rawFindings.title: Missing guard lets `use()` middleware run on invalid non-path URLs
rawFindings.explanation: The new unconditional `var c = path[layerPath.length];` executes even when `layerPath.length === 0`, which makes `path` the empty string only after `getPathname(req)` has succeeded. For middleware mounted at `'/'`, this change causes the prefix-stripping block to be entered unconditionally, and requests with invalid or non-path URLs (for example `req.url = '*'` or `'foo'`) can now be routed into middleware instead of falling through to `done` as before.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the `if (layerPath.length !== 0)` guard around both the separator check and the prefix-trimming block so middleware mounted at `'/'` does not bypass path validation.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: `router.use(function(req,res){res.end()})` with `router.handle({ url: '*', method: 'GET' }, ...)` now reaches the middleware and ends the response instead of skipping the layer and invoking `next`/`done`.
